name: California
rule: immediately, at the time of discharge

name: Colorado
rule: immediately

name: Massachusetts
rule: in full on the day of discharge

name: Montana
rule: immediately when separated for cause or laid off, unless a written personnel policy extends it to the next regular payday or 15 days, whichever is first

name: Minnesota
rule: immediately on the employee's written demand; in default 24 hours after it

name: Connecticut
rule: by the next business day

name: District of Columbia
rule: by the next working day

name: Hawaii
rule: at the time of discharge, or not later than the next working day

name: Oregon
rule: by the end of the next business day

name: Idaho
rule: by the next regular payday or within 10 days (weekends and holidays excluded), whichever is sooner; within 48 hours (weekends and holidays excluded) of a written request

name: Illinois
rule: by the next regular payday

name: Maine
rule: by the next established payday

name: New York
rule: by the payday on which the next pay would have been due

name: North Carolina
rule: by the next regular payday

name: North Dakota
rule: at the regular payday for the periods worked

name: Oklahoma
rule: by the next scheduled payday

name: South Carolina
rule: within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday, which may not be more than 30 days away

name: South Dakota
rule: by the next regular payday

name: Wyoming
rule: by the next regular payday

name: New Hampshire
rule: within 72 hours of the termination

name: Vermont
rule: within 72 hours of the discharge

name: Alaska
rule: within 3 working days after the day of termination

name: Delaware
rule: on the later of the next regular payday and 3 business days after the last day worked

name: Texas
rule: by the sixth day after the discharge

name: Arizona
rule: within 7 working days or by the end of the next regular pay period, whichever is sooner

name: Washington
rule: at the end of the established pay period

name: Kentucky
rule: by the next normal pay period or 14 days after the separation, whichever is later

name: Iowa
rule: by the next regular payday for the pay period in which the wages were earned

name: Kansas
rule: by the next regular payday on which the employee would have been paid

name: Maryland
rule: on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued

name: Michigan
rule: on the regular scheduled payday for the period in which the employee is discharged
law: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act (1978 PA 390)

name: New Jersey
rule: by the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended

name: Pennsylvania
rule: by the next regular payday on which the wages would otherwise be due

name: Virginia
rule: on or before the payday the wages would have been paid had employment continued

name: West Virginia
rule: by the next regular payday on which the wages would otherwise be due

name: Tennessee
rule: by the next regular payday or 21 days after separation, whichever is later
